result.rationale: In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff wraps the axios token call in refreshOAuthTokens(...). In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the result of fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT,...), i.e. a fetch Response, while the surrounding code still does `tokenInfo.data.error` — data is undefined on a fetch Response, so a TypeError occurs. The same mismatch also affects `!tokenInfo.data` checks and subsequent `.data` access. Mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: In sync mode `tokenInfo` is a fetch Response rather than an axios response, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws a TypeError reading 'error' of undefined. Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes whenever credential sharing is enabled, failing Bigin calendar sync at the first expired token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e., a `Response`. In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is assigned from `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then the code does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`. A `fetch` `Response` does not have a `.data` property (axios does), so in sync mode `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and reading `.error` will throw. The diff also passes `credentialId` as the `userId` argument, which is truthy, so the sync-mode branch will be taken whenever sharing + endpoint are set.
